$$\boxed{|T|+|M|\le 18m+30\qquad(m\ge2).}$$
The proposed 15-black-selection versus 15-white-hole local inequality is false. The repair is to prove a slightly larger local inequality and then switch checkerboard colors when that inequality permits a one-unit deficit. Those arguments are explicit sums of nonnegative inequalities; no finite-search maximum is used as a premise. \qquad

The first uses actual matching capacities. The second uses only retained occupancy and the selected-degree condition.The two complementary global counting arguments give

$$P\cap Q\hookrightarrow P\cap N(Q),$$

$$\sum_{w\in Q}p_w\le\sum_{b\in N(Q)}p_b. \tag{M}$$
Here  $N(Q)$  is the complete grid neighborhood. No endpoint is allowed to borrow a mate already used by another endpoint.Four consequences are sufficient for (L1).2.1 Top capacityTake

N(Q)=\{00,02,11,20,22,31\}.$$
